# PRESS RELEASE

## Headline
[One sentence that states the launch clearly. Benefits over features.]

## Subheading
[One sentence that reinforces the headline with a key metric or timeframe.]

## Summary
[Two to three paragraphs in past tense describing what the team built and shipped. Lead with the customer problem, then the solution, then the result. No feature lists. Example: "Today we launched X. Customers told us Y was broken. We built Z. Early results show Q."]

## Problem
[One paragraph describing the customer pain before this launch. Be specific. Quote real customer feedback if available.]

## Solution
[One to two paragraphs describing the experience customers have now. Write as a story, not a spec. No feature lists. No bullet points. Answer: what does the customer do differently?]

## Customer Quote
[A believable quote from a real-sounding customer. This is the truth test — if you cannot imagine a real person saying this, rewrite it.]

> "[Customer quote]"

## Executive Quote
[A quote from the responsible leader describing why this matters to the business.]

> "[Executive quote]"

## How to Get Started
[One paragraph. Describe the single most important action a customer takes to begin using this. Keep it to one step.]

## Internal FAQ

### Q: How does this affect our business model?
A: [Revenue model, pricing changes, impact on existing products. Be honest about trade-offs.]

### Q: What happens at 10x scale?
A: [Architecture, cost, operational load at 10x current traffic. Show you thought about scale.]

### Q: What is the biggest risk that could kill this?
A: [Single point of failure, external dependency, regulatory risk. One risk, clearly stated.]

### Q: What dependencies does this have?
A: [Internal teams, external services, data sources, licenses. List what must exist for this to work.]

### Q: How do we measure success?
A: [Three metrics max. Leading indicator (adoption), lagging indicator (business impact), quality indicator (customer satisfaction). Include targets and timeline.]
